Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both wake views. I’ll use the fish-control shelf only through its stated invariant-transfer protocol, and I’ll keep the implementation to one candidate in `solver/`.

I’m applying two workspace skills: `read-wake-visual-signals-first` to ground the diagnosis in both 3D views, and `fish-control-primitives` because this request explicitly requires its structured transfer protocol. I’ll read their instructions before proposing or editing any controller.

The four sampled rollouts all satisfy the direct-uniform still-water contract and all capture, so there is no sampled termination failure in this batch. I’m treating the slightly better prefill capture as the best finite example and the repeated `0.749242L` capture as the more fragile comparison, then I’ll use inherited left-domain near-misses as the informative failure lineage.

The prefill’s near-goal course-response residual produced only a `0.000152L` deeper boundary crossing, delayed capture by one solver step, left the mean-distance integral effectively unchanged, and preserved the same visible route and wake. That is not a semantic improvement. The reusable lesson will close this terminal course-residual branch; the next candidate needs a distinct observed-response mechanism rather than more near-capture amplitude.

The next candidate will use a different feedback selector, not a gain increase: inside the existing approach/miss corridor, persistent body-frame course error will smoothly arbitrate the beat-scale line-of-sight selector. On the parent trace, those selectors conflict in 38% of samples below `1.75L` and again in 11 of the final 47 samples, including the terminal step; this can make the successful line-of-sight residual briefly steer against the still-large projected miss. Outside that corridor the evaluated controller remains exact.

Both required artifacts are now updated. The candidate changes only the near-goal selector semantics; the durable guidance records the parent residual as a negative result and explains why its tiny first-crossing difference should not be optimized further. I’m moving to deterministic contract, symmetry, locality, and checker validation—no CFD.

The mandated checker was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this ChatGPT account. I’ve read its exact three checks and will run them separately myself, as the inherited workers did.

The first check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same guidance example as the prefill twice. I’m correcting the duplicate label to “duplicate sample,” matching the inherited checker repair pattern; this does not alter solver behavior or optimizer guidance.

All three configured checks now pass locally: guidance delta, finite two-joint Julia contract/schema, and solver editable-boundary. I’m adding one focused counterfactual audit to verify the intended invariants: exact far-corridor pass-through, material activation on a terminal selector conflict, and lateral reflection equivariance.

The counterfactual checks confirm the mechanism is localized and symmetry-safe: it changes 366 reconstructed parent states, all below `1.75L`; every farther command is exact, and reflected terminal states negate both joint commands. I’m doing the final completeness pass now.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1).

It adds near-goal arbitration between beat-scale line-of-sight feedback and persistent body-frame course error while preserving the proven carrier and safety guards.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1), including the bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:163), recording the terminal residual’s negative result and falsification boundary.

Guidance, Julia contract/schema, editable-boundary, locality, and reflection-equivariance checks pass. The configured checker was invoked but its pinned model was unavailable, so its exact checks were run locally. No CFD was run.
